items.title: Section: Marks Five and Six Close the No-Lineage Catalogue

items.zh: 謂彼或時於善說法毘奈耶中暫得出家、或為國王所逼迫故，或為狂賊所逼迫故，或為債主所逼迫故，或為怖畏所逼迫故，或不活畏所逼迫故。非為自調伏、非為自寂靜、非為自涅槃、非為沙門性、非為婆羅門性而求出家。既出家已，樂與在家及出家眾共諠雜住。或發邪願修諸梵行，謂求生天，或餘天處。或樂退捨所學禁戒，或犯尸羅，內懷朽敗，外現真實；如水所生雜穢蝸牛，螺音狗行。實非沙門，自稱沙門；非行梵行，自稱梵行。如是亦依過去、未來、現在世別。當知如是不住種姓補特伽羅，假相出家；非不樂學補特伽羅，名真出家，受具足戒，成苾芻性。由此異門，由此意趣，義顯於彼本非出家，唯有任持出家相狀，墮出家數。是名第五不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。復有所餘不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。謂彼少有所作善業，或由於身、或語、或意；一切皆為希求諸有。或求當來殊勝後有，或求財寶，或求殊勝所有財寶。是名第六不住種姓補特伽羅無種姓相。如是等類，有眾多相。成就彼故，墮在不般涅槃法數。
items.en: Such a person may, at some point, obtain temporary ordination within this well-taught Dharma and discipline — coerced by a king, coerced by fierce bandits, coerced by a creditor, coerced by fear, or coerced by fear of destitution — never for the sake of subduing oneself, quieting oneself, or attaining nirvāṇa. …Having thus gone forth, that person delights in dwelling amid noisy crowds of householders and renunciants alike. Or forms a misguided vow to cultivate pure conduct merely in order to be reborn in a heaven, or some other heavenly realm. Or delights in abandoning the precepts undertaken, or transgresses moral discipline — inwardly rotten, outwardly appearing genuine, like a filthy snail formed in water — a voice like a conch-shell, conduct like a dog: not truly a renunciant, yet calling oneself one; not truly practising pure conduct, yet calling it so. This is called the fifth mark. Such a person performs only a little wholesome action — through body, speech, or mind — and every bit of it is done in pursuit of continued existence: seeking an excellent future rebirth, or seeking wealth, or seeking especially excellent wealth. This is called the sixth mark. Beings of this kind display many such marks; possessing them, such beings fall into the category of those who cannot attain nirvāṇa.

items.title: Section: The Fourth and Final Part of the Ground of Spiritual Lineage Opens — Twenty-Three Types of Person

items.zh: 云何安住種姓補特伽羅？謂住種姓補特伽羅，或有唯住種姓，而未趣入，亦未出離。或有安住種姓，亦已趣入，而未出離。或有安住種姓，亦已趣入，及已出離。或有軟根，或有中根，或有利根。或有貪行，或有瞋行，或有癡行。或生無暇，或生有暇。或有縱逸，或無縱逸。或有邪行，或無邪行。或有障礙，或無障礙。或遠，或近。或未成熟，或已成熟。或未清淨，或已清淨。
items.en: What is a person who abides in lineage? A person who abides in lineage may: abide in lineage alone, not yet having entered [the path], and not yet freed [from affliction]; or abide in lineage, having already entered, but not yet freed; or abide in lineage, having already entered, and already freed. Such a person may have weak faculties, moderate faculties, or sharp faculties. May be greed-dominant, hatred-dominant, or delusion-dominant in conduct. May be born without leisure, or born with leisure. May be heedless, or free of heedlessness. May follow wrong conduct, or be free of wrong conduct. May be obstructed, or unobstructed. May be distant, or near. May be unripened, or already ripened. May be impure, or already purified.

items.zh: 云何名為安住種姓補特伽羅，唯住種姓，而
items.en: What is called a person who abides in lineage, abiding in lineage alone, yet

items.title: The Full List of Twenty-Three, and the First Three: Not Yet Entered, Entered but Not Free, Both Entered and Free

items.zh: 未趣入，亦未出離？謂如有一補特伽羅，成就出世聖法種子，而未獲得親近善士、聽聞正法，未於如來正覺正說法毘奈耶獲得正信，未受持淨戒，未攝受多聞，未增長慧捨，未調柔諸見。如是名為唯住種姓，而未趣入，亦未出離補特伽羅。云何名為安住種姓，亦已趣入，而未出離補特伽羅？謂前所說所有黑品相違白品，當知即名安住種姓，亦已趣入補特伽羅。而差別者，謂猶未得所有聖道及聖道果煩惱離繫。云何名為安住種姓，亦已趣入，及已出離補特伽羅？謂如前說。而差別者，已得聖道及聖道果煩惱離繫。
items.en: May follow wrong conduct, or be free of wrong conduct. May be obstructed, or unobstructed. May be distant, or near. May be unripened, or already ripened. May be impure, or already purified. …It is like a person who possesses the seed of the supramundane noble dharma, yet has not yet drawn near a good teacher or heard the true Dharma, has not yet attained pure faith in the Dharma and discipline rightly taught by the perfectly awakened tathāgata, has not yet upheld pure discipline, has not yet gathered extensive learning, has not yet cultivated growing generosity, and has not yet tamed and softened [wrong] views. This is called a person who abides in lineage alone, not yet having entered, and not yet freed. …Whatever stands opposed to the "dark" category just described is the "bright" category, and should be understood as precisely a person who abides in lineage and has already entered. The distinction is that such a person has not yet attained the noble path and the noble fruit's freedom from the bonds of affliction. …The distinction here is that such a person has already attained the noble path and the noble fruit's freedom from the bonds of affliction.

items.title: Weak Faculties, and the Three Kinds of Wisdom That Track a Practitioner's Growth

items.zh: 云何軟根補特伽羅？謂有如是補特伽羅，於所知事、所緣境界，所有諸根極遲運轉、微劣運轉。或聞所成、或思所成、或修所成作意相應。謂或信根，或精進根，或復念根，或復定根，或復慧根，無有堪能、無有勢力通達法義，速證真實。是名軟根補特伽羅。
items.en: What is a person with weak faculties? It is such a person for whom, regarding what is to be known and the objects of contemplation, all the faculties operate extremely slowly and feebly — whether in attention associated with hearing-wisdom, reflection-wisdom, or cultivation-wisdom. That is: the faculty of faith, the faculty of effort, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, or the faculty of wisdom — none has the capacity or the power to penetrate the meaning of the Dharma, or to swiftly realise what is genuinely true. This is called a person with weak faculties.

blocks.text: The catalogue of "no lineage" ends; then the treatise lists twenty-three kinds of person on the path.

One without lineage may go forth, but "coerced by a king, by bandits, by a creditor, by fear, by fear of destitution", never for the sake of taming oneself. And in practice such a person, like a hollow conch, makes the right sounds without substance. (The image of a tree with hard bark and no heartwood comes from the *Pīxún jì*, not the treatise.)

The list includes those who abide in lineage only, those who have entered, those who are freed; those of weak, moderate, and sharp faculties; those dominated by greed, hatred, delusion, pride, or discursiveness; those of balanced temperament and of slight affliction; those near and far from nirvāṇa; ripened and unripened; purified and unpurified.

items: **In lineage, not yet entered, not yet freed:** one with the seed who "has not yet drawn near a good teacher or heard the Dharma".
**Entered, not yet freed:** one who has begun.
**Entered and freed:** the arhat. Master Cháng Bǎi: when all 128 ropes of the three realms are untied, "one has truly let go and the mind is utterly cool".

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: "if one studies the Dharma without striving to change oneself by it, that cannot count as entry."

In one of weak faculties, faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom all operate slowly and feebly. Such a person relies first on wisdom born of hearing, which can only follow what it is told; then on wisdom from reflection, which can sift the definitive from the provisional; then on wisdom from cultivation (Master Cháng Bǎi).

quiz.q: According to the fifth mark, how does such a person go forth?
options: temporarily, coerced by a king, bandits, creditors, fear, or fear of destitution — never for self-taming, peace, or nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "Coerced by a king, coerced by fierce bandits, coerced by a creditor, coerced by fear, or coerced by fear of destitution — never for the sake of subduing oneself, quieting oneself, or attaining nirvāṇa." Master Cháng Bǎi: in India monastics were outside the law, so creditors could not pursue them.

quiz.q: The simile is "like a filthy snail formed in water, a conch's voice and a dog's conduct"; the English adds "or the bark of a hollow tree." Where does that come from?
options: from the Pixunji's "like a great tree" glossing inner rot — not the treatise; Cháng Bǎi: a conch's voice and a dog's conduct means fine appearance but base behaviour
quiz.why: The Chinese has no hollow-tree simile; it comes from the *Pixunji*'s gloss "like a great tree with a fine hard bark." Master Cháng Bǎi: "a conch's voice and a dog's conduct" describes a fine appearance but base behaviour.

quiz.q: Into what three kinds does the treatise first divide those abiding in lineage?
options: in lineage only, not entered or freed; entered but not freed; entered and freed
quiz.why: "Some abide in lineage alone, not yet having entered and not yet freed; some have entered but are not yet freed; some have entered and are freed." Venerable Miào Jìng: not entered means no faith in the Dharma yet; not freed means practising with faith but not yet liberated.

quiz.q: "未出離" is rendered "not yet having gone forth," easily read as ordination. What do the masters say 出離 means?
options: freedom from the afflictions of craving and views — Cháng Bǎi: untying all 128 ropes of the three realms; Miào Jìng: practising with faith but not yet liberated is "not yet freed"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when all 128 ropes of the three realms are untied, one has truly let go and the mind is utterly cool. Venerable Miào Jìng: "not yet freed" is practising with faith but not yet liberated. The English "gone forth" later becomes "freed" in §44 — inconsistent.

quiz.q: How does the treatise describe one who "abides in lineage only, not yet having entered"?
options: possesses the supramundane seed but has not met a good teacher, heard the Dharma, gained faith, kept discipline, gathered learning, grown in generosity, or softened views
quiz.why: "A person who possesses the seed of the supramundane noble dharma, yet has not yet drawn near a good teacher or heard the true Dharma, has not yet attained pure faith… has not yet tamed and softened views." Master Cháng Bǎi: such a person may even have contacted Buddhism, but only following others in burning incense.

quiz.q: How does the treatise define a person with weak faculties?
options: one whose faculties of faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom operate extremely slowly and feebly, without power to penetrate the Dharma or swiftly realise truth
one with poor eyesight and hearing
quiz.why: All the faculties operate extremely slowly and feebly — whether the faculty of faith, effort, mindfulness, concentration, or wisdom — none has the capacity or power to penetrate the meaning of the Dharma or swiftly realise what is true. Venerable Miào Jìng: contemplating non-self for ages without it taking hold — that is "extremely slow."

quiz.q: The treatise says the weak are slow whether in hearing, reflection, or cultivation. How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish hearing-wisdom from reflection-wisdom?
options: hearing-wisdom cannot discern; reflection-wisdom can sift the Dharma and tell definitive from provisional
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one with hearing-wisdom lacks the ability to discern; one with reflection-wisdom can sift the Dharma, knowing what is definitive or provisional. Cultivation-wisdom relies on the text yet also not, because it has actual experience.
